Our goal is to leverage NASA’s open datasets, machine learning, and advanced software architecture to build scalable, high-performance tools that address the 'Next Frontier' of space technology."
summary: Field Shift is an offline-first, multilingual precision agriculture platform designed to protect smallholder farmers from climate volatility and monoculture soil degradation. By translating NASA Earth observations (SMAP soil moisture, MODIS vegetation indices, POWER agroclimatology, and NEX-GDDP climate projections) into field-specific recommendations, Field Shift generates dual-horizon crop rotations optimized across four pillars: restoring soil organic nitrogen, interrupting botanical pest cycles, conserving water via daily FAO-56 evapotranspiration modeling, and maximizing net farm profit through real-time mandi prices. Built for remote edge environments, Field Shift operates completely offline with IndexedDB local sync, features vernacular voice audio narration in 30+ regional languages, and provides human-readable agronomic justifications for every suggestion.
details:
1. What Does It Do or How Does It Work?

Rotara is an offline-first, satellite-informed crop rotation suggestion engine engineered for smallholder Indian farmers, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), and agricultural extension agents.

The End-to-End Workflow:

  1. Interactive Parcel Boundary Mapping: The farmer defines their field boundary on an interactive GPS satellite map. Turf.js calculates exact acreage and coordinates in real time.
  2. Soil Health Card Digitization (OCR): Instead of manual typing, the farmer uploads or photographs their government Soil Health Card. An on-device optical character recognition (OCR) pipeline extracts Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), Potassium (K), soil pH, and Organic Carbon.
  3. Just-in-Time (JIT) NASA Climatology: When a rotation plan is requested, the engine queries the NASA POWER API for 10 years of daily historical agrometeorological data (precipitation, growing degree days, solar radiation, temperature) centered on the farm’s exact latitude and longitude.
  4. Agronomic Constraint Solver:
  • Soil Envelope Filter: The crop's pH and texture tolerance are checked against the farmer's soil card; unsuitable crops are immediately disqualified (UNSUITABLE_PH).
  • Botanical Family Break: Prevents planting crops from the same family back-to-back (e.g., Solanaceae after Solanaceae) to break pathogen and pest life cycles.
  • Biological Nitrogen Credit: Identifies nitrogen-fixing legumes following heavy-feeder cereals (e.g., Chickpea after Maize) and computes the exact chemical urea saved per acre.
  • Multi-Criteria Optimization: Ranks 2- to 3-season crop sequences based on a composite score: Soil Improvement (40%), Water Deficit Risk (30%), Pest Break (15%), and Economic Margin (15%).
  1. Dual-Engine Offline Fallback: If the internet disconnects in rural fields, a client-side rotation engine running in Dexie.js (IndexedDB) takes over instantly to deliver local recommendations without a network round-trip.
  2. What Benefits Does It Have?
  • Reduces Chemical Fertilizer Costs: Quantifies nitrogen fixation credits (e.g., saving 8–15 kg of synthetic urea per acre) by rotating pulses after cereals.
  • Mitigates Drought & Climate Risk: Matches crop water demand curves against 10 years of NASA monsoon trends, steering farmers away from high-water crops during dry cycles.
  • Breaks Pest & Disease Cycles: Systematically enforces family breaks, naturally lowering pesticide expenses.
  • Reverses Soil Degradation: Replenishes micro/macronutrients and builds organic matter across multi-year rotations.
  • Maximizes Farm Income: Cross-references rotation sequences with real-time Agmarknet Mandi commodity prices to maximize market margins.
  1. What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?
  • Environmental Impact: Halts soil acidification and chemical runoff into groundwater across intensive agricultural belts (e.g., Punjab, Maharashtra, Karnataka). Promotes regenerative agriculture without requiring costly commercial inputs.
  • Socio-Economic Impact: Democratizes precision agriculture for marginal farmers owning less than 2 hectares. Enables FPOs to aggregate planting schedules across member plots to avoid localized market gluts and negotiate better harvest prices.
  • Food Security & Climate Resilience: Equips rainfed and dryland farmers to adapt to erratic monsoons, heatwaves, and seasonal shifts driven by climate change.
  1. What Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, or Software Were Used?

Frontend (PWA): React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, Vite, Framer Motion, Dexie.js (IndexedDB), Workbox (Service Worker), Turf.js, Tesseract.js, Lucide Icons. Backend API: Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy (AsyncIO), Alembic, Pydantic v2, Celery, Redis 7. Spatial Database: PostgreSQL 16 with PostGIS 3.5 for geometric parcel indexing, boundary polygons, and centroid queries. Cloud & Deployment: Google Cloud Run (serverless Suggestion Engine), Google Compute Engine (backend container VM), Google Cloud Build, Firebase Hosting (PWA edge CDN). Satellites & External APIs: NASA POWER (daily agrometeorology), NASA SMAP (soil moisture), Agmarknet (mandi prices), Open-Meteo.

  1. How Is Your Project Creative?
  • Zero-Barrier Soil Digitization: Farmers do not need expensive IoT soil probes or lab tests. Rotara digitizes existing paper government Soil Health Cards using in-browser computer vision.
  • Just-In-Time (JIT) Satellite Ingestion: Instead of storing terabytes of heavy satellite rasters, Rotara queries 10-year NASA agrometeorological time series on demand in ~1.2 seconds, keeping cloud infrastructure lean and scalable.
  • Dual-Engine Hybrid Architecture: Combines a cloud-native solver on Cloud Run with a lightweight, browser-based IndexedDB engine. It bridges the gap between high-performance cloud computing and rural realities with zero internet.
  • Farmer-Centric Metrics: Rather than outputting abstract indices, it calculates direct farmer benefits: "Saved 8.0 kg Nitrogen / acre" and "Breaks Solanaceae pest cycle for 3 seasons".
  • Voice-First Vernacular Accessibility: Full translation matrices for English, Hindi, and Marathi, complete with Devanagari text-to-speech audio guidance for low-literacy users.
  1. What Factors Did Your Team Consider?
  • Intermittent Rural Connectivity: More than 70% of Indian farms experience intermittent or zero mobile data connectivity. Offline-first PWA caching and client-side database fallback were mandatory architectural constraints from day one.
  • Economic Constraints of Smallholders: Smallholder farmers cannot invest in high-cost hardware. Rotara relies entirely on freely accessible satellite observations and existing government cards.
  • Indian Cropping Calendars: Rotations are explicitly built around Indian agricultural seasonality (Kharif, Rabi, and Zaid), accounting for regional crop durations and irrigation access (rainfed vs. irrigated).
  • Language & Literacy Diversity: Complex technical jargon is replaced by visual radar charts, color-coded health badges, and voice readouts in local languages.
  • Agronomic Rigor & Guardrails: The system enforces hard biological limits. A crop will be rejected if soil pH or drainage characteristics violate its survival envelope, ensuring farmers never receive unrealistic recommendations.
